title: SAT-ACT: Learning CDCL Branching from Outcome-Derived Action Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2610.41290v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Learning-based approaches have increasingly been explored for SAT solving, with particular attention to improving branching decisions in conflict-driven clause learning (CDCL) solvers. These approaches derive branching guidance either from static structural properties of SAT formulas or from dynamic signals obtained through solver feedback and execution traces. However, these forms of supervision provide limited evidence about state-dependent branching effects, while different outcome measures may favor different branching choices. To address these limitations, we propose SAT-ACT, an outcome-derived learning framework for CDCL branching. We design three complementary outcome comparison criteria to extract action preferences from independent branching action rollouts initiated at the same solver state. translated_title: SAT-ACT：从基于结果的动作偏好中学习CDCL分支策略
translated_abstract: 基于学习的方法在SAT求解中的应用日益受到关注，其中特别关注改进冲突驱动子句学习（CDCL）求解器中的分支决策。这些方法要么从SAT公式的静态结构属性中获取分支指导，要么从通过求解器反馈和执行轨迹获得的动态信号中获取分支指导。然而，这些监督形式对于状态依赖的分支效果所能提供的证据有限，而且不同的结果度量可能会偏好不同的分支选择。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了SAT-ACT，一个面向CDCL分支的基于结果的学习框架。我们设计了三种互补的结果比较准则，从在同一求解器状态下启动的独立分支动作rollout中提取动作偏好。这些准则识别出有结果支持的偏好，并在证据不足或相互冲突时保持比较结果未定。
tldr: 提出SAT-ACT框架，通过三种互补的结果比较准则从同一求解器状态下的独立分支动作rollout中提取动作偏好，从而学习更优的CDCL分支决策策略。
en_tdlr: SAT-ACT is an outcome-derived learning framework that extracts branching action preferences from independent rollouts at the same solver state using three complementary outcome comparison criteria, improving CDCL branching decisions in SAT solving.
